one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-23 to 2026-11-22. No AT&T earnings (next late January 2027) and no ex-dividend date (last was Oct 9; next ~early January). Scheduled: Verizon Q3 on Oct 26 and T-Mobile Q3 on Oct 28. These are the main sources of news on wireless pricing; Verizon has been buying share with flat wireless service revenue, so a strong Verizon add number is a modest negative for T and a soft one a relief. Unscheduled but likely: SpaceX's own quarterly report/updates on Starlink Mobile and FCC steps on the SpaceX-Grain 800 MHz deal; each recent SpaceX headline cost T 8-11% in a day, so the left tail is fatter than usual. Against that, the stock is down 16.8% in a month to near its 52-week low (Trefis) after an EPS beat and raise, where short-horizon reversal and the 5.3% yield attract buyers. Net: centred at ~$21.0 (flat to slightly up), monthly sigma ~9.5% vs the usual 30%/3.5 = 8.6%, slightly fatter tails.

fair_value.method: Driver-led 3-year build (subs x ARPU for wireless and broadband, AC cost and capex drivers) valued at the horizon on NTM figures: 6.2x EV/EBITDA ($23.17, weight 0.5), 8.5x P/E on own EPS $2.90 ($25.51, 0.3) and a 12% FCF yield on $2.87/share ($24.77, 0.2) = research target (12m) $24.19.

Q4-25 net adds ~0.52M), +~1.17M Lumen customers 2 Feb 2026 (16,248 - 1,999 - 13,080), quarter-ends 14.85/15.48/16.25M, Dec-26 ~16.95M (Q4 net adds ~0.70M) -> time-weighted average 15.55M. 2027: net adds 2.5M (Q3 2026 run-rate 769k/quarter, fiber build to 60M+ locations by 2030) -> avg 18.2M; 2028: net adds 2.4M -> avg 20.65M.

Cost = driver revenue - EBIT.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY2025 capex $20,842M (F51) + vendor financing $1,181M (Q4 2025 Ex.99.2) = $22.0B; 9M 2026 capital investment $16,786M (Q3 2026 Ex.99.3); guide $23-24B 2026, $22-23B 2027-28 (Q3 2026 release) | 2026: 9M $16,786M + Q4 ~$6.6B = $23.4B (inside the $23-24B guide). 2027 $22.7B and 2028 $22.6B: inside the lowered $22-23B guide, upper half because the record (2024 $22.1B vs $21-22B guide) runs slightly above and fiber build plus the Lumen footprint stays heavy. See guidance_check.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: 8.5x NTM adjusted EPS $2.9 (own build: FY2027 $2.62, FY2028 $2.96; Zacks $2.54/$2.86) + adjustments per share $0.86

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Cross-check only: peer-median NTM P/E 11.1x x consensus NTM EPS $2.80 (Zacks blend) = $31.1. Not used: the median is pulled up by TMUS/RCI/European names with lower leverage; AT&T has not traded at the peer median in the past decade.

bear.story: Starlink Mobile (EchoStar AWS-4/H-block + Grain 800 MHz, terrestrial build) and a Verizon volume push start a price war in 2027: all-in wireless ARPU 2.5% below base, subs -1%, broadband connections -3%; the market prices AT&T near cable (5.3x EBITDA, 7.6x EPS, 13.4% FCF yield) and questions buybacks at 3.1x leverage.

base.story: Wireless service grows ~2-2.5% on 1.0-1.2M postpaid phone net adds and flat-ish ARPU; fiber + Internet Air add ~2.5M connections a year; AC EBITDA +5.5-6%; Legacy fades; Mexico sold; ~$7.5B/yr buybacks; multiples hold at today's de-rated levels (6.2x / 8.5x / 12%).

bull.story: SpaceX's US mobile plan proves niche (satellite-first coverage, limited terrestrial sites), wireless pricing holds, convergence lifts net adds; FCF tracks the $19B+/$21B+ guide and the multiple recovers toward the pre-October 6.8x level (6.9x / 9.2x / 11%).

comps_summary.peer_range: EV/EBITDA NTM 4.1-6.8x (9 peers); P/E NTM 2.5-13.4x (8 with meaningful EPS)
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 6.2x EV/EBITDA NTM (EV incl. NCI and preferred; ~5.8x on the peers' EV-without-NCI basis) sits at the peer median (6.0x) and just below the wireless-led subset (VZ 6.4x, TMUS 6.0x, BCE 6.3x, RCI/TU 6.8x); 8.5x P/E is below the 11.1x median, at VZ's 8.7x.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium claimed. The P/E discount to the median is structural: AT&T carries 3.1x net leverage and ~$1.5B a year of NCI/preferred claims ahead of common, and has traded at 7-9x adjusted EPS through the cycle, as VZ does; the median is lifted by TMUS (faster growth) and lower-leverage Canadian/European names. Only 9 peers: the US has three national wireless carriers and two large cable operators; LUMN (distressed enterprise wireline after selling its consumer fiber to AT&T), TDS/SHEN (thin coverage) and Deutsche Telekom (consolidates TMUS, double count) are left out.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$16.5 (about 5.3x NTM EBITDA, cable-like, and a ~6.7% dividend yield) the market would be pricing a structural wireless price war or a dividend/buyback cut, not volatility: it would mean either Starlink Mobile pricing or Verizon/cable promotions are taking all-in wireless ARPU down (our bear case) or that FCF is tracking well below the $19B+ guide. Watch: postpaid phone adds below ~200k a quarter with ARPU falling, or a 2027 FCF guide under $18B.

reverse_dcf_check: At 6.2x NTM EBITDA (~$50.3B) the EV of ~$312B against unlevered FCF of ~$25B (EBITDA - $22.6B capex - ~$3B cash tax) is an ~8% unlevered FCF yield, which at a ~7% WACC implies about -1% a year perpetual change in unlevered FCF after 2028 (0% at ~8%): flat-to-slightly-declining revenue and margins once the fiber build ends, i.e. the multiple already prices meaningful share/price loss to Starlink Mobile and cable, which we think is plausible rather than conservative.

sbc_treatment.note: FY2025 stock comp $536M (F43). AT&T adjusted EPS, adjusted EBITDA and FCF do not add SBC back, so the EBIT, EPS and FCF used here are after SBC; the share count falls only by buybacks net of ~20M shares a year of issuance. Peers (VZ, TMUS) report adjusted EBITDA before SBC in some cases; at 0.4% of AT&T revenue the basis gap is ~0.05x EBITDA and is ignored.

reasoning: Evidence (primary documents first): Q3 2026 release and exhibits (Oct 21): revenue $32.3B (+5.3%), adj. EBITDA $12.5B (+5.4%), adj. EPS $0.65 vs $0.54, FCF $5.0B; 379k postpaid phone adds (vs 405k a year ago), churn 0.92%, record 769k fiber+Internet Air adds. GAAP diluted EPS $0.13 (F27: $0.12) carries $3.37B of impairments/restructuring: a $2.6B ($0.41) non-cash impairment on Mexico wireless, held for sale after the Oct 13 agreement to sell it for $2B, plus $0.09 employee-separation charges and $0.02 other (Ex.99.3). Guide: 2026 adj. EPS raised to ~$2.40 (partly lower Mexico depreciation), EBITDA upper part of 3-4%, FCF $18B+, 2027-28 capex cut to $22-23B, FCF $19B+/$21B+, $24B+ buybacks 2026-28, leverage 3.13x after the $23B EchoStar spectrum (closed late July) returning to ~2.5x in 2029. Price moves: Oct 9 (-10.8%) followed SpaceX's Oct 8 agreement to buy Grain's nationwide 800 MHz portfolio for Starlink Mobile (TMUS fell ~13% too), which changes the multiple (long-dated pricing risk), not the 2027 earnings path; Oct 21 (-6.4%) was results day: the postpaid phone add miss and the cut capex/working-capital framing mattered more than the EPS raise; a small earnings-path change (we trim wireless ARPU growth); Oct 23 (-8.0%) followed reports that SpaceX wants access to ~80,000 cell sites (terrestrial build), again a multiple/long-dated effect (single press source: Trefis; we could not find the original report). Model: driver-led build, 6 drivers: postpaid phone subs (74.95/76.28/77.38M avg), all-in wireless ARPU ($77.74/78.21/78.52 vs $76.42), fiber+Internet Air connections (15.55/18.2/20.65M avg), broadband ARPU ($63.05/63.5/64.5, after -4% in 2026 from the Lumen mix), an AC cost driver giving AC EBITDA +6.2/+5.5/+6.0%, and capital investment $23.4/22.7/22.6B. Legacy -25% a year with EBITDA turning negative in 2028 (company), Mexico gone from Q2 2027. Result: adj. EBITDA $48.2/48.7/50.7B (consensus $48.3/49.8/52.0B: we are 2% lower on wireless pricing), EPS $2.38/2.62/2.96, FCF $18.8B 2027 (guide $19B+). Guidance record: AT&T met or beat its first EPS guide 3 of 3 years (median +2.7%) and FCF 3 of 3 (median +3.75%); we stay near the guides but a little below on FCF and EBITDA growth because the guides predate the SpaceX moves and Verizon's volume push (Verizon guides 2-3x more phone adds in 2026 with flat wireless service revenue). Valuation: EV/EBITDA 6.2x (0.5; peers median 6.0x, wireless-led peers 6.0-6.8x; we keep the post-SpaceX de-rating instead of the 6.8x pre-news level), P/E 8.5x on own NTM EPS $2.90 (0.3; VZ 8.7x), FCF yield 12% (0.2) -> research target (12m) $24.19 (engine base). Bear $16.65 (price war: ARPU -2.5%, 5.3x), bull $29.28 (threat fades, ~6.9x). Ladder: the engine's scenario mix (median $23.8, q25-q75 $19.5-27.8) averaged with a plain lognormal around ~$23 at the stock's 30% realised vol, because the stock is in a headline-driven regime where our edge on the SpaceX question is small; median ~$23.4, i.e. ~12% upside plus a 5.3% dividend. Not driver-linked: the stated NTM EPS and FCF/share on the P/E and FCF-yield legs (they move with scenarios via eps_pct). Data limits: Bigdata.com, Alpha Vantage and Twelve Data were unavailable, so consensus came from Nasdaq (Zacks) and MarketScreener pages; full Q3 call transcript text was not reachable (MarketBeat summary used); the 10-Q MD&A was not in the fetched text.

drivers.label: Advanced Connectivity operating costs including D&A (revenue less segment operating income)

bear.story: Starlink Mobile (EchoStar AWS-4/H-block + Grain 800 MHz, terrestrial build) and a Verizon volume push start a price war in 2027: all-in wireless ARPU 2.5% below base, subs -1%, broadband connections -3%; the market prices AT&T near cable (5.3x EBITDA, 7.6x EPS, 13.4% FCF yield) and questions buybacks at 3.1x leverage.

base.story: Wireless service grows ~2-2.5% on 1.0-1.2M postpaid phone net adds and flat-ish ARPU; fiber + Internet Air add ~2.5M connections a year; AC EBITDA +5.5-6%; Legacy fades; Mexico sold; ~$7.5B/yr buybacks; multiples hold at today's de-rated levels (6.2x / 8.5x / 12%).

bull.story: SpaceX's US mobile plan proves niche (satellite-first coverage, limited terrestrial sites), wireless pricing holds, convergence lifts net adds; FCF tracks the $19B+/$21B+ guide and the multiple recovers toward the pre-October 6.8x level (6.9x / 9.2x / 11%).

model_inputs.structure_note: Driver-led 3-year build (FY2026-28; FY2028 is the year the horizon NTM reads). Six drivers compute Advanced Connectivity revenue (89% of FY2025 revenue = driven share), its EBIT, and capital investment: postpaid phone subs x all-in wireless ARPU (plus equipment/business fiber/other at the FY2025 per-sub ratio of $484.88/yr, a calibration constant), fiber+Internet Air connections x ARPU, an AC cost driver, and capex. Legacy (6.7%) and Latin America+Corporate (3.8%) are plain segments with cited paths. Value is carried by an NTM EV/EBITDA leg (0.5), a P/E leg on our own NTM adjusted EPS (0.3) and an FCF-yield leg on our own NTM FCF/share (0.2); no DCF (policy). Stated EPS and FCF/share are used because the engine's P/E and FCF legs would not deduct the ~$1.5B a year of NCI income/distributions and preferred dividends. Net debt at the horizon is stated (cash taxes are far below book in 2026-27 under OBBBA, so the engine's FCFF at a 22% book rate would understate deleveraging). The stated EPS and FCF/share are not driver-linked (they move with scenarios through eps_pct).
model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (1) the 6.2x EV/EBITDA keeps today's SpaceX de-rating (pre-news 6.8x); (2) the Forged Fiber stake at book ($2.58B) is a low-confidence derived split of held-for-sale net assets; (3) the $8.1B postemployment (OPEB) obligation and the pension (about 95% funded after the $1.5B contribution, Q2 2025 release) are not treated as debt, the usual telecom convention; (4) spectrum purchases beyond EchoStar (e.g. an upper C-band auction) are not in the base. fair_value.value is the engine base horizon value.
